articleTitle: Antenna System Requirements and Challenges Towards 6G - An Industrial View
abstract: 5G is currently being rolled-out in many countries and nationwide networks with successive provisioning of new communication capabilities and services will keep the industry busy for many years. However, academia and industry have initiated research on fundamentals of the next generation of wireless communication (6G). In this paper, we will discuss challenges to realize flexible and cost-effective antenna systems for these next generation communication systems. The focus will be on the antenna and antenna system requirements and challenges from an industrial view and particularly on the millimeter wave (mm-wave) and sub-THz frequency range.

articleTitle: On the Impact of an Antenna Field of View on the Classification of UAVs
abstract: Detection and classification of Unmanned Air Vehicles (UAV s) at a distance have become important because of the potential threats of the illegal usage of them. Radar systems are preferred for UAV s detection because of their advantages over other UAVs detection systems. In this paper, an investigation of the effect of an antenna Field of View (FoV) on Machine Learning (ML) accuracy is conducted. A full-wave Electromagnetic (EM) CAD tool is used to generate the required datasets for this investigation. Five UAV s were used in this work, a fixed-wing, a helicopter, two quadcopters, and a hexacopter UAVs. The ML algorithm was trained on a relative angle of 0° between the UAV s and the antenna, and it was tested on relative angles of 20°, 40°, 60°, 80°, and 90° between the UA V s and the antenna. The ML classification accuracy decreases with the increase of the relative angle between the UAV s and the antenna. The accuracy of a classifier can be estimated by employing Multiple-input Multiple-output (MIMO) radars to detect the Angle of Arrival (AoA) of drones and the relative angle between the drones and the antenna.

articleTitle: On-chip mmWave Slot Antenna Arrays with Improved Radiation Efficiency
abstract: A 60 GHz coplanar folded slot antenna (CFSA) using a deep air cavity with a back reflector is proposed. The single element CFSA operates at 60 GHz with a -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 6.49% (58.1-62.0 GHz). The presence of air cavities and reflectors serves to improve efficiency and realized gain. At 60 GHz, the peak gain of the proposed CFSA antenna is found to be 6.85 with a directivity of 7.05 dBi. The efficiency of the single element antenna is simulated to be 95%. The maximum mutual coupling between array elements is determined to be -12.19 dB. The mutual impedance and array characteristics of the CFSA extended into a linear array were analyzed. The sixteen-element linear CFSA array is simulated to have a 16.29 dBi array gain with a radiation efficiency of 90%. The scan angle in the azimuth direction is demonstrated. It is characterized by 11.07 dBi array gain at -60°beam steering angle using fixed sequential phase delays.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization for efficient end-fire superdirective array design
abstract: This paper presents a simple multi-objective optimization procedure, for efficient end-fire superdirective array design. The proposed method includes simultaneously the array directivity as well as its radiation efficiency in the optimization process. The proposed method, is used afterwards to design a three electrical dipoles based array operating at 780 MHz, for various separation distances in the range <tex>$[0.03\lambda, 0.2\lambda]$</tex>. At <tex>$0.05\lambda$</tex>, the antenna array presents a maximal directivity of 7.3 dBi, which is still 0.5 dB above the Harrington limit, a radiation efficiency of 99% and an IEEE gain of 7.2 dBi. To avoid using a feeding network, a parasitic array was formed where the second element is excited while the first and the third ones are loaded. The parasitic antenna exhibits practically the same results as the fully driven case.

articleTitle: A Compact Wideband Millimeter-Wave Beam-Scanning Antenna Array for Industry 4.0 and Beyond Applications
abstract: In this paper, a compact wideband series-fed 8-element linear antenna array is designed that covers the entire unlicensed 60 GHz band from 57–71 GHz. The linear 1 ˟ 8 array has a simulated −10 dB impedance bandwidth of 35.21% (50.53 to 72.13 GHz). The peak realized gain of 8-element array is 13.3 dBi at 60.5 GHz. The gain variation is less than 1 dB from 57–66 GHz and the overall gain is above 11.5 dBi up to 71 GHz. Side-lobe levels are below −10 dB in both E and H-planes, with low cross-polarization levels. The proposed array also manifests frequency-dependent beam-scanning in the elevation plane (y-z plane) from −10° to +35°. The proposed array is suitable for millimeter-wave industrial applications which require high bandwidth and multi-gigabits-per-second data rate. The designed array can work on various 60 GHz communication protocols such as IEEE 802.11ad, IEEE 802.11ay, IEEE 802.15.3c, Wireless HD and ECMA-387.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Off-Body Communications with Grooved GP
abstract: A low profile circularly polarized (CP) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed for off-body communications. The challenge of achieving a precise DRA-feed alignment has been addressed by incorporating a second ground plane with a groove, in which the DRA is placed. The impact of the human body presence has been investigated using CST. The antenna offers a measured gain of 8.7 dBic at 28 GHz together with impedance and axial ratio (AR) bandwidths of 29% and 14%, respectively. Measurements and simulations are in close agreement.

articleTitle: mmWave Mobile Devices with Reconfigurable Broadside and Endfire Radiation using Shared Aperture Antenna-on-Display and Antenna-in-Package
abstract: This paper is the first to propose a collection of shared aperture concept using Antenna-on-Display (AoD) and Antenna-in-Package (AiP) to independently and collectively maximize high gain beam steering coverage for mmWave mobile devices. The proposed AoD and AiP are exemplified to demonstrate this approach to obtain miniaturized dimension while achieving enhanced beam coverage. The proposed AoD operates at 5G FR2 n261 (27.5-28.35 GHz) and n260 (37–40 GHz) while supporting dual polarization. The AoD further maximizes the boresight coverage in the direction normal to the display panel The devised AiP combines end-fire and broadside antennas as a shared aperture cavity slot antenna structure to minimize the antenna dimension at 28 GHz band. By integrating the proposed AoD and AiP within mobile devices, beamforming coverage can be enhanced by achieving hemisphere radiation pattern with minimum and maximum gain of7 dBi and 9.56 dBi respectively (based on four-element array), and 50 % CDF of more than 4.2 dB compared to that of an independent AoD configuration.

articleTitle: Scattering performances of Metasurfaces affected by Electromagnetic Phase Roughness
abstract: In this contribution, we study and fully characterize the reduction of the scattering gain when the electromagnetic reflection response of a reflective metasurface is not perfect as designed but affected by a random variation of its surface properties. Here, we consider a metasurface able to reflect a plane wave impinging from 0 = -20° towards the direction θ=+40° and affected by a pure-phase electromagnetic random roughness. We characterize the metasurface response introducing a statistical approach describing how much the electromagnetic roughness alters the desired functionality of the MTS under inspection. A proper set of numerical simulations agrees very well with the analytical results, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed statistical model.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Surfaces in Reverberation Chambers for Over-the-Air Mobile Device Testing
abstract: While mode-stirred reverberation chambers are useful for over-the-air (OTA) testing of mobile devices, they have the disadvantage of providing limited control over the spatial properties of the fields incident on the device under test. However, if one or more of the chamber walls are modified with a reconfigurable surface, the chamber mode weighting can be optimized to achieve specified field spatial characteristics. This paper combines method of moments and finite-difference time-domain electromagnetic models of such a chamber with optimization tools that allow both design of the physical chamber and determination of the operational parameters of the reconfigurable surfaces required to achieve the desired field characteristics. Results from these tools demonstrate the potential of this technology for modern OTA testing.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Tri-modal Electromagnetic Structure for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
abstract: In this paper, a large-scale electromagnetic (EM) structure is designed and demonstrated for collecting ambient cellular power between 930 to 960 MHz. The novelty of the EM structure is that it is scalable in terms of size or gain, and can produce three high-gain radiation beams pointing to three different directions simultaneously. The construction of the proposed large-scale EM structure consists of a tri-modal patch antenna acting as the basic radiating element. Then, four basic elements are concatenated by three custom-made feed networks forming a 3-port sub-array. When the sub-arrays are linked together into an array and the corresponding three ports are subject to different phase weightings, the EM structure is capable of harnessing low power ambient RF energy concurrently with three different incident angles.

articleTitle: The Potential of Context-Aided Communications
abstract: With the fifth generation mobile communications (5G) and its evolutions towards 6G, users will make use of bandwidth-demanding services like augmented reality and virtual office applications, also on the move. In this context we discuss the potential of integrated sensing and communications, with a focus on context-aided communications. We revisit some of our recent results and describe future potential research directions.

articleTitle: Maximum Gain of an Electrically Small Cosines-Dipole-Based End-Fire Array
abstract: Electrically Small Antennas (ESAs) are of high interest in applications where a compact size wants to be preserved. With the objective of the realization of a highly efficient and superdirective array within a very compact space, a new radiating element and array design is proposed, optimized for maximum attainable gain. A cosines-dipole printed antenna is designed by adjusting the amplitude and periodicity of the cosine microstrip, to resonate at the desired frequency of 916 MHz. Then, to achieve high gain two elements are closely spaced, mirrored to their excitation point, one fed and the other parasitic. An analytical method for gain optimization based on the Spherical Wave Expansion (SWE) theory is used to maximize the array gain. Two different array geometries are compared by looking at the power distribution of the spherical modes, and the configuration that returns the highest gain is chosen. A realized gain of 6.5 dBi is achieved in simulation, for a total size included in a radiansphere of <tex>$\boldsymbol{ka}=\mathbf{1}$</tex>, with the advantage of having a printed antenna, thus planar, easy to integrate, and low cost. The proposed antenna solution presents in theory an excellent trade-off between electrical size and realized gain.

articleTitle: Metasurface 2-D Leaky-Wave Antennas Fed by Multiple Sources
abstract: Leaky-wave antennas are nowadays very popular. They have been proposed for several applications, such as communication systems, tracking, and remote sensing. A plethora of designs have been studied and characterized, based on different technologies and configurations. We consider here a special type of leaky-wave antenna based on the use of metasurfaces, which defines a Fabry-Perot cavity, fed my multiple sources. A previous design proposed by some of the Authors is briefly reviewed and some ongoing developments are presented.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Metagratings for Efficient Anomalous Reflection
abstract: We develop a rigorous scheme for designing effective metagratings (MGs), sparse composites of subwavelength polarizable particles (meta-atoms), based on low-cost dielectric substrates featuring non-negligible losses. To this end, the common analytical model governing these devices is adapted to consider lossy substrates, and additional degrees of freedom are introduced in order to enhance the device performance. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach by designing a FR4-based anomalous reflection MG, verified via full-wave simulations. These results pave the path to the realization of efficient beam manipulating low-profile constructs with reduced cost, harnessing the high-fidelity analytical model to provide insight and point out practical avenues to overcome loss limitations in diverse material sets across the electromagnetic spectrum.

articleTitle: A wave physics approach to electronically steerable antennas
abstract: Electronically steerable antennas (ESAs) are compact, thin, and light antennas. ESAs are being more and more used for Satcom applications thanks to the rapid development of mega-constellations and the advent of 5G with mmWave. However, many limitations still exist in the current designs. Indeed, all designs up to date rely on the same old concept of phased arrays, which are composed of many sources phased matched to point in different directions. These arrays can be passive, in the sense that a common feed is used to radiate through many radiators, or active in which case each tiny emitter contains its own source of waves. The formers are poorly efficient because they are very dissipative but relatively simple and low-energy greedy. On the other hand, the latter provide good performances but they are extremely costly and use huge amounts of electrical power to operate. Additionally, a significant amount of power is lost as dissipation. Finally, both active and passive phased arrays have tremendous problems that need to be overcome before they are vastly used. Here we introduce the concept of leaky reconfigurable cavity antenna, which stems from a fundamentally different unique approach to beamforming. It makes use of a thin leaky cavity that, when excited by single or several feeds, can create any desired wavefield and consequently any desired radiation pattern. To achieve this desired radiation pattern, the cavity is reconfigured in real-time by electronically reconfigurable metasurfaces (MMs). The MM controls the reflections of the waves inside the cavity, acting as a software-controlled set of boundary conditions. Being based on discrete components, the antenna maintains the cost-efficiency, robustness, and power sobriety of the simplest passive phased arrays, with a power needed for beamforming as low as a few tens of watts at K<inf>u</inf> or K<inf>a</inf>. Furthermore, since the control is solely based on electronics, it achieves the performances of active phased arrays at the same time, for instance in terms of gain or switching speeds. With its high performance and low complexity, our concept paves the way for the deployment of electronically steerable antennas at scale. In conclusion, since the beamforming does not result from the synchronization of many elementary sources, but rather from the shaping of a wavefield inside a cavity, our concept is standard or protocol agnostic, it can support multiple frequency bands, and emit multiple beams, at different frequencies, with different polarizations and an optimal scan loss.

articleTitle: Link Budget Considerations for Reflecting Intelligent Surfaces in Radio Channels
abstract: Applying reflecting intelligent surfaces (RIS) in a communication channel paves the way to smart electromagnetic environments. The design modalities for reconfigurable meta-surfaces generating anomalous reflections are introduced. These meta-surface based RIS are evaluated for their usability in communication channels. A comparison is made with the state-of-the art technology: classical relaying stations. From this, the resulting requirements for the design of a RIS from a channel perspective are determined. An example set up in an realistic urban scenario as well as computational results are provided. It is shown that RIS, if properly designed, are a real alternative to relaying stations.

articleTitle: Liquid-Dielectric-Based Patch Antenna with Polarization and Frequency Reconfiguration
abstract: In this work, a novel tuning concept is proposed for patch antennas with reconfigurable polarization and center frequency tunability. The proposed tuning concept is based on a cavity-based dielectric substrate whose dielectric properties are tuned by altering the height of a liquid dielectric (LD) within four air-filled cavities. Specifically, when two diagonal cavities are filled with LD, right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) or left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) can be obtained with wide impedance matching. Furthermore, by filling with LD two adjacent cavities, linear polarization (LP) can be realized. It is shown that by tuning the height of the LD in the LP mode of operation continuous center frequency tuning between 3.3 to 4.0 GHz can be achieved while obtaining good radiation pattern characteristics. The cross-polarization of the antenna in the LP state is lower than -25 dB for all tuning states, and the gain loss is less than 0.15 dB when compared with a static patch antenna built on the same substrate.

articleTitle: A calibration procedure for two-antenna direction of arrival finding systems
abstract: Under the background of satellite communication, this paper presents a different method of finding the direction of a signal by using a system of two identical pyramidal horn antennas with frequency selective surfaces type structures applied in the horn aperture. Based on a calibration in an anechoic chamber, in the far field zone, a correction factor was calculated to compensate the effects of the individual radiation pattern asymmetry, the discrepancies between the characteristics of the antennas, and mutual coupling.

articleTitle: Comparison of Additively Manufactured Dual-Polarized Probe Antennas at Ku-Band
abstract: This paper presents a comparison between two additively manufactured dual-polarized open-ended waveguide probe antennas. The probe antenna design covers the <sup>u</sup>p-link and down-link frequencies of satellite communications at Ku-band (10.7 - 14.5 GHz), and it could be used for fast ground-station antenna measurements. The used fabrication processes are the fused filament fabrication (FFF) followed by the metallization with conductive paint and the direct metal printing using binder-jet process. The measured performance of the manufactured prototypes agrees well with the simulated performance in the design frequency range. The slight dimensional deviations from the design values increase the low-frequency coupling and reflection coefficients compared to the simulations. To decrease the coupling between polarizations, a horn-type waveguide opening is introduced.

articleTitle: A Simple Decoupling Method for Millimeter-Wave Aperture-Coupled Patch Antenna Arrays
abstract: This work presents a decoupling method for aperture-coupled patch antenna arrays, especially for millimeter-wave applications since the method is simple in both principle and structure. There is no additional decoupling structure, and the decoupling is achieved by constructing a decoupling path between the feeding line of an element and the feeding aperture of the adjacent element to cancel the original mutual coupling. Although no decoupling operation is utilized between non-adjacent elements, the coupling between them is also reduced. Full-wave simulated results of an example working at 27.5 GHz are provided to verify the effectivity of the decoupling method, from impedance matching, coupling suppression, and radiation performance point of view.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna with Circular Polarization on Dual WiMAX Bands Based On Liquid Metal Switching Capability
abstract: In this article, we present a novel reconfigurable antenna with circular polarization on dual WiMAX bands (3.5, 5.8 GHz) based on liquid metal switching capability. The circular polarization reconfiguration is achieved by connecting the rectangular parasitic element (Pc) with the feed line by the liquid metal switch. The mechanism of switching is based on controlling the liquid metal in microfluidic channels by applying a voltage to move and remove the high-conductivity liquid metal EGaIn on the microchannel. The proposed antenna has a simple configuration and compact size that generates dual WiMAX band with Circular polarization (CP) performance by changing the state of the liquid metal switch that is suitable for 5G wireless technology.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Band Antenna With Even- and Odd-Mode Resonances for 5G Mobile Applications
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile dual-band antenna integrated with the back cover of the mobile device is presented for fifth-generation (5G) terminal applications. The proposed antenna element is composed of two pairs of perpendicular metal strips, a coupling feeding probe, and a parasitic shorted patch. By using the proposed feeding structure, the even and odd modes can be excited on the metal strips simultaneously, which can cover two working bands. Meanwhile, to further improve the working bandwidth, a parasitic resonance on the shorted patch is also utilized. Finally, a four-element multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is designed and discussed. As a result, the proposed MIMO antenna can cover 3.40-4.02 GHz and 4.75-5.00 GHz. The isolation is higher than 15 and 21 dB in the lower and higher bands. And the total efficiency is also higher than 48% in the working bands, while the calculated envelope correlation coefficients (ECCs) are lower than 0.15.

articleTitle: A Dielectric Lens Antenna with Reconfigurable Scanning Beams for K-Band Wind Profile Radar
abstract: A multibeam lens antenna with high gain and low sidelobe is presented in this paper. Based on the high gain and defocusing scanning characteristics of the dielectric lens, a fixed 15° beam scan is achieved by switching the feeds at different zones. By introducing the Abbe sine condition into the lens shaping design, a K-band shaping medium lens is designed, which achieves ultra-low sidelobes while scanning the beam. The feed consists of five corrugated horn antennas with symmetrical rotation around the central axis, which have axially symmetrical pattern and very low sidelobe level. Therefore, it is very suitable for feeding a lens antenna system. The simulation results show that in K band, the reflection coefficient is below −25 dB, the radiation efficiency is more than 90%, the maximum gain is 31 dBi, and the sidelobe is below 20 dB. The antenna has simple structure, strong stability and low manufacturing cost, which can be applied to mmWave wind profile radar.

articleTitle: A Wide-Beam Dielectric Resonator Antenna Based on Complementary Excitation Source
abstract: In order to accurately detect and identify the target signal, the antenna is required to have the performance of wide- beam coverage. In this paper, a millimeter-wave wide-beam dielectric resonator antenna based on the principle of complementary excitation sources is proposed. It is mainly composed of two layers. The lower layer is the traditional slot array antenna, which can be equivalent to the magnetic current source along the y-axis direction. The upper layer is composed of a dumbbell meta material array, which can be equivalent to the current source along the z-axis direction and the current source along the x-axis direction. Three different excitation sources can generate complementary patterns. By properly adj usting the size of the antenna, the wider beamwidth can be obtained. Finally, a wideband wide-beam antenna operating at 30 GHz was designed and discussed. The operating bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 27.9 to 32 GHz, the maximum gain is 5.5 dBi, and the half-power beamwidth of the E-plane radiation pattern is 183°.

articleTitle: 2.5D Inductive Intertwined Frequency Selective Surface For Pass-Band Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design of a miniaturized intertwined pass-band inductive frequency selective surface in a 2.5D configuration. In the literature, we have identified that the 2.5D configuration has been described and used only for a capacitive intertwined frequency selective surface; therefore, we describe the design of this structure, taking Brigid's cross as an example that later on can be used as starting point for other types of structures. Moreover, the proposed structure presents high miniaturization capabilities, reaching a period of 0.00967 wavelengths and a fractional bandwidth of 30.856 % without the influence of a substrate. Finally, besides the pass-band capabilities of the structure, it also offers a wide stop-band in upper frequencies with a fractional bandwidth of 73.15 %.

articleTitle: Fast Prototyping of an L-band Array Using Additive and Subtractive Techniques
abstract: A well performing and novel L-band array for GPS application is designed for fabrication using primarily additive manufacturing. The aperture is comprised of inverted-F antennas (IFAs) fabricated by copper plating 3D printed elements in stereolithography. To achieve right-hand circular polarization, a three-layer meanderline polarizer (MLP) is designed and integrated in a hybrid fashion with 3D printed low-permittivity “foam-like” spacers built by fused deposition modeling. The base plate and supporting frame are also 3D printed with the former covered in aluminum foil to achieve RF grounding for the entire system. To further reduce prototyping time, a superstrate, placed between the IFAs and the first MLP layer is fabricated in-house using conventional subtractive machining. The MLP layers are copper etched on Kapton though can be realized using conductive trace printing in future works. Measurements and simulations show active mismatch loss < 0.5 dB, axial ratio < 2 dB, and aperture efficiency > 63% at the GPS L1, L2, and L5 bands with dual-band axial ratio < 3 dB bandwidth from 1.075-1.275 and 1.5-1.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband Dual-Polarized Vivaldi Base Station Array Antenna for 5G Smart Networks
abstract: We present here a Quasi-Omnidirectional dual polarized antenna working from 1.6 up to 3.8 GHz for 5G technology. The antenna has the overall dimensions of π × 1352 × 50 mm<sup>3</sup>. The Vivaldi antenna was chosen as the element of the array due to its wideband impedance bandwidth, high gain and the end-fire radiation patterns characteristics.

articleTitle: Novel Techniques Applied to MIMO Antenna Array for 5G Sub-7 GHz Smartphone Applications
abstract: As many modern cities have recently embraced the 5G communication system, its related antenna designs for smartphones operating in the 5G New Radio (NR) band (n77/n78/n79) are vital to the 5G user experience. In this Invited Talk, dualband/multiband and wideband 5G antenna designs with MIMO array technology that can cover the entire 5G NR band n77/n78/n79 (3300–5000 MHz) are initially introduced. To further fulfill the new 5G specifications NR-U (New Radio Unlicensed) Band n46 (5150–5925 MHz) and n96 (5925–7125 MHz), various novel MIMO array antenna design techniques for achieving the entire Sub-7 GHz are uncovered with detailed diagrams to reveal the logic behind each design technique.

articleTitle: A Compact Hybrid Liquid Antenna for Wi-Fi Applications
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid antenna is introduced for multi-band applications. The proposed antenna overcomes the problems associated with designing dual/multi-band antennas with a compact size of <tex>$\leq ^{1}/_{2}\lambda_{0}$</tex> in the overall dimensions. A liquid dielectric resonator antenna and a ME - dipole configuration is considered together for this to realize multi-mode operation achieving decent broadside gain and efficiency.

articleTitle: Transformation Optics and Prior-Knowledge-Guided Deep-Learning-Enabled Synthesis for Microwave Metalens Antennas (Keynote)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of recent advances in metalens antenna modeling and synthesis. First, we discuss the application of true transformation optics (TTO) to Luneburg lenses, which enables compact antenna design without degrading radiation performance. The transformed lens antenna maintains the feed on/near the lens surface, a key feature of Luneburg lenses. We implement the lens antenna using anisotropic metamaterials. Next, we propose a deep learning-enabled synthesis method that incorporates prior knowledge to design pixelized metasurface unit cells and metasurface lens antennas. This method increases design freedom and expands the unit cell database, leading to enhancements in phase shift range and gain bandwidth. Our approach is demonstrated through the greatly improved gain bandwidth of a metalens antenna.

articleTitle: Convex Body-Surface Curvature Influence on the On-Body Path Gain - a Numerical Investigation
abstract: A numerical study of the influence of convex surface curvature on the path gain for a configuration that consists of a dielectric slab and two open-ended S-band waveguide antennas is presented. The curvature is varied from 0.0 1/m to 5.0 1/m. In the first part of the sweep range, there exists a line of sight between the two antennas, whereas for the last part they are located in each other's shadow zone and the wave propagation relies exclusively on diffraction, i.e., creeping waves. It is found that across the entire sweep range the path gain decreases linearly with an increase in curvature on a logarithmic scale and the total decrease is about 15 dB. Furthermore, the presence of creeping waves is verified for a curvature value where no line of sight exists.

articleTitle: Balanced Duplex Filtering Dielectric Resonator Antenna with High Isolation Performance
abstract: A balanced duplex filtering dielectric resonator antenna (DF-DRA) is proposed in this paper. This proposed DF-DRA combines the functions of the antenna, the filter and the duplexer into one highly integrated multifunctional module. The designed dual-mode rectangular DRA operating as a common radiation structure is excited by two cross slots etched on the top of a dual-mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity. The dual-mode SIW cavity is fabricated and worked as a common filtering element. Then, the SIW cavity is fed by two pairs of differential input/out ports on the bottom layer, which not only suppresses the unwanted common mode (CM) noise but significantly improves the isolation between the lower and higher channel. The synthesis co-design methodology is utilized to process the integration design. Measured results show that the balanced DF-DRA can operate with differential mode (DM) 10dB impedance bandwidth of 2.5% (5.15-5.28 GHz) and 3.4% (5.69-5.89 GHz) for two channels, respectively. The measured DM peak realized gains are 5.18-5.91 dBi and 5.11-6.57 dBi at two channels. The DM channel isolation is up to 60dB.

articleTitle: A Broadband Dipole Antenna Implemented with Solar Cell
abstract: This paper presents a broadband fat dipole antenna made from a solar cell for dual functions of wireless communication and energy harvesting. For this purpose, the dipole elements of the antenna were made from a copper- indium-gallium-selenide-based solar cell; hence no extra structure was used for the antenna. This approach resulted in a very low-profile and simple solar cell antenna structure. A coaxial cable that was connected to the dipole elements was used for feeding. The antenna and the solar cell were made to operate independently of each other using RF decoupler circuits. The gap between the dipole elements was minimized to achieve a high form factor. The proposed solar cell integrated antenna has a broad impedance bandwidth of 94.2%, ranging from 2 GHz to 5.56 GHz. Moreover, the whole structure has a very compact size of 52.5 mm <tex>$\times 25$</tex> mm <tex>$\times 0.571$</tex> mm (0.66 <tex>$\lambda_0 \times 0.31 \lambda_0 \times 0.0071 \lambda_{0}$</tex> at 3.78 GHz), with a form factor of 95.23% and optical transparency of 100%.

articleTitle: Wireless Channel-adaptive Sensor-integrated Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface based on Deep Neural Network
abstract: This paper presents functional reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) with sensing capability that is applicable to various wireless communication environments at microwave, millimeter-wave (mmWave), and potentially sub- Terahertz spectrum. The devised deep-learning-based model enables the sensing system to be consistently applied to any propagation environment. The sensing information is used to redirect the RIS in accordance with the wireless channel condition. Thus, this enables the featured RIS to be cognitive without the need of any external feedback as suggested in various literature in the past. The presented RIS unit cell entails two varactor diodes on the top patch unit cells to enable phase shift of the reflected signal. For ease of implementation, via walls are used to minimize phase distortions due to mutual coupling while reflecting the incoming electromagnetic waves and signals to intended targets while simultaneously sensing the target's location. The proposed methodology is exemplified at 28 GHz using a 10 x 10 unit cells configuration. Measured and simulated results confirm that the deep neural networks have 99 % accuracy in inferring the test data and the devised 1-bit quantization unit cells redirect the signal from 15 ° to 60°. This novel concept ascertains low-cost, practical employment of a truly intelligent RIS for future wireless applications.

articleTitle: A 2-30-GHz MFCW Radar for Vital Sign Detection Using Variable Carrier Frequencies
abstract: This paper presents a concept of vital-sign detection using multiple-frequency continuous-wave (MFCW) radar system. Carrier frequencies from 2 GHz to 30 GHz under three types of thoracic movements are verified by using a broad band multi-channel Doppler radar system. The results show that there are different favorable vital-sign detection frequencies for different respiration conditions.

articleTitle: W-Band Cavity-backed Folded-slot Antenna Using GaAs Integrated Passive Device Technology
abstract: A W-band cavity-backed folded-slot antenna based on GaAs integrated passive device technology is proposed in this paper for the first time. A via-cavity is formed to produce TE<inf>120</inf> mode resonance and suppress surface waves, and an offset folded slot is designed to match the high impedance of the cavity. The simulated and measured <tex>$\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{11}}$</tex> and the simulated radiation patterns are presented, which demonstrate that the antenna can operate from 97.8 GHz to 98.6 GHz with a maximum gain of 2.5 dBi while consuming a small area of only <tex>$\mathbf{0.84}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{1.325}\mathbf{mm}$</tex>. The proposed antenna is suitable for system-on-chip millimeter-wave applications where front-end modules and the antenna are built on the same chip for minimal signal transfer loss.

articleTitle: Antenna Materials Development in Automotive Radars
abstract: Automotive radar sensors are used for various functions, such as blind spot detection (BSD), lane change assistance (LCA), collision mitigation (CM), parking aid (PA), and rear cross traffic alert (RCTA). And the different types of radars are mounted around a car depending on the required functions. Antenna design and materials can be optimized according to the radar types. Recently thermoset materials have started to be used for Print Circuit Board (PCB) antenna for mm Wave applications due to the benefit of simple PCB process, design flexibility and lower cost compared to PTFE. However, the usage of thermoset materials has been limited for car radar antennas because they are generally thermally unstable and have higher loss. By selection of right thermosetting resin system and optimizing resin formulations, we have developed thermoset materials which demonstrate stable Dk/Df after aging at 125C. We confirmed the electric stability at 77GHz using the ring resonator method which considers the effects of dielectric layer, copper foils and the interface between them. The insertion loss of the materials that we have developed is comparable to PTFE materials being used for automotive radar applications.

articleTitle: Filtering Metasurface Lens for Chip-to-Chip Communications in Multicore Multichip Systems
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel approach for chip-to-chip communications in multicore multichip systems. The proposed solution is based on the planar low-profile Maxwell fish-eye metasurface lens with full azimuth coverage which is fed by the coupled-resonator filters. For demonstration, an eight-port 28 GHz filtering metasurface lens is designed and simulated based on the cost-effective additive manufacturing 3D print and PCB-based substrate integrated cavities technologies. The results show promising performance in terms of impedance matching, low insertion loss transmission and low interference/mutual coupling behaviour along with simple, compact, cost-effective and scalable solution compared with previous works.

articleTitle: Connected Dipole Antenna Cluster of Enhanced Spherical Coverage CDF for mm-Wave Applications
abstract: In this paper, we present an antenna cluster concept operating in millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) frequency bands for 5G applications. Unlike conventional arrays made up of identical elements, a cluster array is constructed using non-identical dipoles with high coupling that are placed in a 2-mm wide slot. The cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the spherical coverage gain is used to evaluate the beam-forming capability. High coverage gain over a wide band can be achieved by adjusting the amplitudes and phases of excitation vector. To further enhance the spherical coverage, reactive elements are loaded into the gaps between adjacent dipoles. These reactive elements are selected from a pre-defined database using genetic algorithm-based optimization. The proposed connected dipole cluster demonstrates hemispherical coverage gains greater than 4 dB in the low band (24 to 29.5 GHz) and greater than 6 dB in the high band (37.5 to 43.5 GHz) at the 50%-tile CDF.

articleTitle: Prephase Method for 1-bit Phase Compensation Single-Beam Scanning Reflective Metasurface Design
abstract: In this paper, the prephase method and the prephased unit cell designs for 1-bit reflective metasurfaces are discussed. Focusing on the symmetrical beam in 1-bit reflective metasurfaces under incident plane waves, the prephase method can break the even symmetrical array factor. With random prephase distributions, the symmetrical beam is effectively suppressed, and a single beam is formed. Moreover, the customized prephase distribution with equivalent amplitude tailoring further suppresses the sidelobe levels as beam scanning. For the realization of prephase, two kinds of methods are presented for the prephased unit cell designs. The proposed prephase method and prephased unit cells provide the foundation for 1-bit reconfigurable intelligence surface designs.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Water-Based Antennas
abstract: Water is an inexpensive, abundant and bio-friendly material for many microwave applications. The high permittivity of water at microwave frequencies, as well as its liquid state, enables compact and reconfigurable dielectric resonators, which can be used in antenna configurations and functional material structures such as metasurfaces. In this work, we present two water-based antennas with reconfigurable responses operating in the lower microwave frequencies. First, we present a highly subwavelength antenna operating as a magnetic dipole antenna. The second is a Huygens antenna with an increased directivity due to a balanced excitation of dipole modes. Both numerical and experimental results are presented. The proposed water-based antennas may serve as an easy-to-fabricate and cheap alternative for the VHF and low end of the UHF bands.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Light-Weight Ultra-Wideband Tightly Coupled Array for Sub-6 GHz Applications
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile light- weight ultra-wideband tightly coupled array for Sub-6 GHz applications. The antenna element consists of horizontal and vertical structures, which can be fed directly by the 50 Ω coaxial line, avoiding the expensive and complex baluns. The vertical structure allows the antenna element to achieve wide-angle scanning without using a complex and bulky superstrate layer. To further lower the antenna profile, a portion of the vertical structure is placed horizontally. Ultimately, an infinite array is designed with a 4.8:1 bandwidth (0.62- 3 GHz) and an active VSWR < 3.2 while scanning up to ±45° in the E- and H- planes. Its profile is only 0.09λlow, where λlow is the wavelength at the lowest operating frequency. The proposed antenna has the merit of low- profile, light-weight, ultra-wide bandwidth, wide scanning range, and low cost.

articleTitle: 5G Millimeter-Wave Dual-Band Beamforming Antenna and Wireless Link Tests
abstract: In this paper, a beamforming device is presented to work at two 5G millimeter-wave frequencies. It is a flat structure and is able to transmit and receive wireless signals through two 5G channels now that it takes the form of the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and a duplexing feed is connected to the radiating elements as one piece of equipment. The performance of this novel dual-band antenna is observed with n257 and n260 bands from standpoints of Sii as the return loss for impedance matching, Sij as channel distinction between ports i and j, and antenna gains. Directivity for the beamforming function based on the low impedance mismatch at the frequency bands is given as the simulated and measured data of the antenna under test (AUT). Also, wireless link is built by this antenna system with the capability of channel selection.

articleTitle: Large-Aperture Cavity-Excited Metagrating Antennas for Dynamic Beam Switching
abstract: We present a theoretical approach to devise mul- tiport cavity-excited switched-beam antennas, based on the re-cent concept of metagratings (MGs - sparse arrangements of polarizable particles designed via detailed tailoring of mutual coupling). The discrete nature of the cavity eigenmode basis enables extension of the standard (semianalytical) MG design procedure to allow application of multiple constraints on the same passive composite. Consequently, the static MG is designed to yield a different set of eignemondes on the aperture in response to excitation of different sources (input ports), leading to radiation towards different angles. As verified via commercial solvers, this full-wave-optimization-free scheme yields large-aperture antenna devices with high aperture illumination efficiencies for each of the designated radiation states, providing a simple path to realize dynamic beam steering, especially useful at high frequencies.

articleTitle: W-Band Comb-Line Array Antenna for Wind Turbine Blade Clearance Detection
abstract: This paper proposes a compact, low sidelobe level, high gain and narrow beamwidth W-band comb-line antenna. The transmit and receive antenna arrays are composed of several 14- element series-fed linear arrays and a 1-to-n power divider. The antenna gains are around 20 dBi with sidelobes lower than −20 dB. This pair of antennas can form a MIMO array for radar to detect wind turbine blade clearance.

articleTitle: Aperture-coupled Bowtie Patch Antenna Design for Autonomous Driving Applications
abstract: Autonomous driving will reshape transportation networks, offering at the same time many benefits such as safety, reliable vehicle-to-vehicle communication, and extended telecommunications. For a self-driving vehicle to navigate freely and perceive its environment, it is necessary to be equipped with many sensors. Automotive radars and antenna arrays that operate at 76–81 GHz have been proposed as key elements in future autonomous vehicles. In this work, an aperture-coupled bowtie antenna is designed utilizing hunger games search optimization. The proposed element achieves quite satisfactory values of return loss and gain, as well as broadband operation at 76 GHz - 81 GHz.

articleTitle: Reflectarrays for CubeSat Applications
abstract: Reflectarrays are widely considered prime candidates for high-gain antennas on micro-and nanosatellite platforms, such as CubeSats. For such platforms, the fact that reflectarrays can be constructed using planar surfaces means that they are much easier to stow in the limited launch envelope than traditional reflector antennas, that require curved surfaces to produce high gain. Furthermore, the missions flown on nanosatellite platforms typically require less bandwidth than missions on medium and large satellites which means that the limitations in bandwidth, that are the major drawback of reflectarrays compared to traditional reflector antennas, are less important. TICRA has for the last decade been involved in several projects related to developing reflectarrays for CubeSats. These include projects related both to the development of software for design of reflectarrays and in the development of reflectarray antenna systems, including in a number of projects for the European Space Agency (ESA). In this work, the work carried out at TICRA in the area of Reflectarrays in general and on reflectarrays for CubeSats in particular, will be presented.

articleTitle: Phased Multibeam Antennas Employing Generalized Joined Coupler Matrix
abstract: In this paper, we present a new type of feed networks to feed multibeam antennas, known as the generalized joined coupler (GJC) matrix. Using the GJC matrix, the same phase shifters for each beam can be tuned simultaneously to steer each beam independently. The configuration of the GJC matrices, the theory for synthesizing them and experimental results are reported.

articleTitle: Applications of Artificial Dielectric Layers for mm-Wave Antennas
abstract: Artificial Dielectric Layers (ADLs) have recently been exploited to improve the radiation and impedance performance of integrated antennas at millimeter wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) frequencies. The ADLs are composed by layers of sub-wavelength periodic metal patches that can be arranged within a host medium to synthesize an equivalent anisotropic material. Thanks to the availability of closed-form expressions for the modeling, ADLs can be conveniently designed to realize matching layers and impedance transformers when used in the closed proximity of antennas, to improve their bandwidth and the front-to-back ratio. An overview of different applications that benefit from this concept is given. Moreover, recent developments on the use of ADLs for wideband flat lenses are described.

articleTitle: Impact of Antenna Array Arrangement on MIMO Radar for Human Identification Application
abstract: This paper proposes a human identification technique robust to the subject position deviation using Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar with vertical array arrangement. This method calculates eigenvectors from the training and test propagation channels, which are compared to perform human identification. The vertically arranged array alleviates the positional dependency of the eigenvectors corresponding to the targets. The experiment is carried out on five subjects in an indoor environment. The vertical array achieved a 92% identification rate on average, while the horizontal array achieved the 47% when the training data comprising the signal responses corresponding to multiple positions over the tested area was used for both cases. This result clarified the vertical array yields a recognition rate better than the horizontal array.

articleTitle: High Speed and Resilient Wireless Interconnects in the Near Field
abstract: Bessel beams present the peculiar properties of being non-diffractive and self-healing within the near field of the radiating aperture. These properties are here exploited to establish robust near-field links with error-free transmission at W-band. These links are generated by using two non-diffractive launchers, consisting of spline-profile metallic horns. An appropriate design of the horn enables the generation of a Bessel beam within a distance, called non-diffractive range, which is typically in the near field of the launcher. This contribution experimentally demonstrates non-diffractive Bessel beams generated by a spline profile horn within the launcher's non-diffractive range. Besides, the self-healing feature has been tested by placing a metallic object in front of the transmitting horn. Finally, we have evaluated a near-field link by measuring its bit error rate (BER) with and without the metallic obstructions. An error-free communication has been obtained in both cases for a distance approximately twice the non-diffractive range of one horn and for a data stream of 1Gb/s using an on-off keying (OOK) modulation.

articleTitle: Human-aware Beamforming Method Based on Electromagnetic Field Strength Estimation
abstract: This study proposes a beamforming (BF) method to maximise the received power at the receiver (Rx) in microwave wireless power transfer (MWPT) under the constraint that the human exposure power is maintained below a standard value. The proposed method first estimates the electromagnetic field strength (EMFS) of a human based on a combination of i) equivalent channel estimation between the human and transmitter and ii) human localisation using the same frequency as that of MWPT. Subsequently, a convex optimisation problem was formulated to maximise the received power of the Rx under the constraint that the estimated EMFS on the human must be maintained below the standard value. Solving this problem enables the determination of the optimum BF weight that enables null steering by considering the human area, suppression of human exposure, and high transfer efficiency. The results of full- wave simulations show that the ratio of the received power to the human exposure power of the proposed method is 5.11 dB higher than that of the conventional method, with maximum transfer efficiency that does not consider human exposure, enabling both high transfer efficiency and human avoidance. Furthermore, it is shown that if the angle between the receiver and the human is equal to or greater than 20°, it is possible to suppress human exposure below the standard value in the human body area while maintaining high transfer efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis Results of Single-Layered Reflectarray Antenna with Branch Elements
abstract: A reflectarray antenna (hereinafter “reflectarray”) applies the reflection phase control function of a frequency-selective reflector to a plane reflector. Various beam shapes can be formed by appropriately selecting the mirror surface configuration and shape of the resonant elements. Furthermore, a reflectarray that changes the beam direction depending on the polarization has been reported. Additionally, an element shape that satisfies the conditions for varying the beam direction with polarization has been proposed. In this study, a reflectarray was designed using this element shape, and its performance was evaluated by electromagnetic field analysis.

articleTitle: Robust On-Body Antenna Based on Discretized Planar Surfaces
abstract: This paper presents a novel on-body antenna consisting of discretized metallic patch elements connected with lumped components. The antenna is designed to on-body application, and it could be placed, e.g., to the sling of the backpack. Since most of the human body is composed of water, it has a significant effect on antenna performance. The main effects include detuning of the antenna and a deteriorating radiation efficiency. The proposed antenna inherently resists the detuning effects as compared to a conventional antenna. Therefore, the antenna provides a robust operation in various user scenarios. The details of the structure and element values are optimized with a readily available method that enables the optimization of lumped components to improve the total efficiency. The results show that a 400 MHz bandwidth can be achieved with reasonable efficiency.

articleTitle: Electrically Small VHF Monopole Antenna for Mobile Handset Application using Magneto-Dielectric Material
abstract: Magneto-Dielectric Material is used for the design of an electrically small monopole antenna at the VHF band. By loading partially with MDM along with metallic parasitic element and impedance matching of non-resonant (Small) Monopole, the proposed antenna achieves a miniaturization rate factor of the height greater than 70%, a satisfactory gain for this size and 10% of impedance bandwidth are obtained.

articleTitle: Optical Antenna Array for 6G
abstract: The optical array antenna is designed based on the link budget under the indoor environment for 6G system. The coverage area of the optical array is provided by multi-beam scanning antenna using high gain elliptical beam. This paper describes the link budget, antenna beam shaping for coverage area scanning and multi-beam scanning for efficient spectrum usage

articleTitle: Low-cost Transmit-array Antenna Prototype at Ka-band Combining Low Profile and Mechanical Wide-Angle Beam Scanning
abstract: Transmit-arrays (T As) have been proposed as a cost-effective technology for designing beam antennas capable achieving wide-angle beam steering using only in-plane mechanical movements. As a spatially fed antenna, its performance is limited by the system focal distance. The design requires a rather complex trade-off angle between maximum scanning angle, minimum focal distance and minimum gain considering all beam pointing directions. The authors developed a new iterative method for optimizing the TA phase correction for extremely low focal distances (F/D<0.4). Herein, this general procedure is validated through a prototype comprised of an open waveguide, as a primary source, and a fully dielectric 3D- printed T A. The rectangular aperture dimensions are 195x145x16 mm and the focal source is placed at 50 mm (F/D~0.34). This antenna scans up to 50°, with a gain of 25 dBi at 30 GHz, 1.5 dB of scan loss, SLL< -10 dB and 1 dB-bandwidth of 6.7<sup>%</sup> (29 to 31 GHz).

articleTitle: On-Chip Terahertz Antennas and Arrays for 6G and Beyond
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the research on passive and active on-chip terahertz antennas and arrays conducted at the State Key Laboratory of THz and Millimeter Waves (City University of Hong Kong). For passive antennas, we focus on the performance in impedance and gain bandwidths of the antennas and the size reduction of the feeding networks for the arrays. For active on-chip antennas, we focus on the antenna size, their placement in an array, and the impedance matching to the active circuit to achieve high radiation power.

articleTitle: Contactless Sensing Using Intelligent Walls
abstract: Human activity monitoring is a fascinating field of study that can help the disabled and/or elderly patients to live independently. Different ways have been proposed to identify human activities, including using sensors, cameras, wearables, and non-contact microwave sensing. Microwave sensing has recently attracted a great deal of attention because of its ability to resolve the privacy problems associated with cameras and the discomfort produced by wearables. Existing microwave sensing approaches, however, have the fundamental problem of requiring regulated and perfect conditions for high-accuracy activity detections, which limits their widespread application in non-line-of-sight (Non-LOS) contexts. Intelligent wireless walls (IWW) are proposed to enable high-precision activity monitoring in complicated areas where standard microwave sensing is ineffective. The IWW is a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) capable of beam steering and beamforming and incorporated with machine learning algorithms, can accurately and automatically recognise human behaviours. Two complicated environments were considered for the experiment: a corridor junction scenario in which the transmitter and receiver are located in distinct corridor sections and a multi-floor situation in which the transmitter and receiver are located on various building levels. Three separate bodily movements are evaluated in each of the environments: sitting, standing, and walking. Two individuals, one male and one female, performed these tasks in both scenarios. It is shown that IWW provides a maximum detection increase of 28% in a multi-floor situation and 25% in a corridor junction scenario when compared to conventional microwave sensing without RIS.

articleTitle: Integration of Secure Key Generation and Data Encrypted Communication in Wireless Environment
abstract: Physical-layer secret key generation (SKG) provides high-level security for data encryption in wireless communications, using the shared unique channel state information between legal partners. Most of SKG schemes focused on only SKG itself, while the combination of SKG and encrypted data transmission using the generated secret keys needs to be explored. Here, we propose and demonstrate a secure wireless communication scheme, where SKG and encrypted data communication are integrated together. For SKG, the randomness originated from the input data is utilized to increase the effective key generation rate (KGR) up to 20.8Kb/s when the input data rate is 250Kb/s. Afterwards, the data is encrypted using the generated secret keys and advanced encryption standard (AES). The feasibility and robustness of the integrated system have been verified by the experimental results. Compared with the system where SKG and encrypted data communication are separated, the time required to transfer the same amount of data will be reduced by 48.04%.

articleTitle: X-Band Circularly Polarized Antenna for CubeSat Communication
abstract: A compact size high gain circularly polarized patch antenna with polarization diversity is presented for CubeSat communication. The antenna has polarization diversity and could support both Right-Hand Circular Polarization (RHCP) and Left-Hand Circular Polarization (LHCP) at the same time. The impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 27% (7.1GHz – 9.4GHz) which is represented by the S<inf>11</inf> result. The axial ratio of the proposed antenna is 23% (7.2GHz – 9.1GHZ) and the gain is 5.5 dBic. The radiation pattern of the antenna convenient for CubeSat is also provided.

articleTitle: Over-The-Air Automotive Radar System Testing
abstract: Testing automotive radar systems becomes more and more significant due to the safety critical decisions taken by radar systems in vehicles. With increasing vehicular autonomy in levels 3 to 5, the necessary system tests increase significantly before incorporating the radar system into the advanced driver assistance system. High effort is being made to move the system tests from the road to the labs, as being already the case for hardware-and vehicle-in-the-loop test systems. The paper at hand addresses investigations of different shapes of radar test system front-end antenna configurations. It is shown that in a bi-static front-end setup, the transmitting and receiving antenna shall be placed as closely together as possible in order to avoid angular discrepancies between physical target angle and evaluated target angle by multiple-input multiple-output radar systems under test.

articleTitle: Integratable Antenna Concepts Based on Conformal Antennas for 3D Radar Systems
abstract: The performance parameters of radar modules can be significantly increased by using 3D antennas. Today there are different concepts and different manufacturing technologies for 3D antennas under discussion. The aim of this publication is to derive an approach to match the appropriate 3D antenna packaging technology to the application and to achieve the best performance from the radar module. Examples for different technological approaches will be discussed.
